article_title: Teaching Aids a Special Pedagogy Tool of Brain Development in School Children, Interest and Academic Achievement to Enhance Future Technology
citation: Joseph, O. C. (2015). Teaching Aids a Special Pedagogy Tool of Brain Development in School Children, Interest and Academic Achievement to Enhance Future Technology. Journal of Education and Practice, 6(29). https://www.iiste.org
title: Interest Inventory Test (IIT) and Academic Achievement Test (AAT) instruments
description: The researcher designed two ten-item instruments: the "Inte rest Inventory Test (IIT) to measure the children i nterest" and the "Academic Achievement Test (AAT) to measure the chil dren academic achievement level". Both were validated by three professors from three universities and pilot tested with fifty children outside the study population. Reliability was 0.71 for the IIT (Cronbach Alpha) and 0.79 for the AAT (Kuder-Richardson formula 20).
requirements: Administration with the assistance of class teachers, pre-tested before teaching and post-tested after
constraints: Reliability values of 0.71 and 0.79 were obtained from a pilot with fifty children not part of the study population
examples: Both instruments were administered as pre-tests and post-tests to the 400 pupils across the ten schools
